purpose: Repair the failed typography layer without rolling back photographic or visual-direction gains. Generate each Chinese title as one coherent wordmark system before per-glyph detailing.

preservation_lock.mother_reference: R1C-APPROVED-SHANYEJI-CANONICAL.jpg remains the sole mother reference for this family

anti_rollback_rule: A user criticism applies to the named failing layer by default. Do not invalidate or regenerate already-improved layers unless the user explicitly rejects those layers too.

what_improved: Current photography/base imagery is visibly better than earlier stages and must be retained.
The distilled typography route showed more design intent than the ordinary baseline in the first blind review.
what_failed: Typography remains far below the approved Shanyeji mother-reference level.
The first T1 distilled attempt damaged glyph correctness.
The one technical correctness retry restored readability but broke wordmark coherence: paired characters looked like different design languages assembled together.
problem_statement.formal_boundary: Do not interpret typography failure as total-project failure. Do not rerender photography or restart the entire visual system.

compiler_change.principle: Design 豆坊 or 茶作 first as one graphic mass with a shared visual genome; individual glyph personality is introduced only after the whole-word system is coherent.

five_high_leverage_variables.definition: One shared logic for stroke weight range, terminal shape, curvature/angle family and corner behavior across all characters in the wordmark.
The complete two-character title must read as one memorable outer contour at thumbnail scale before internal detail is judged.
Spacing, overlap, alignment, near-contact and mass distribution are designed at word level; characters may differ but must visibly belong together.
Counters and gaps form a related rhythm across the whole title instead of independent holes or arbitrary cuts inside each glyph.
Each glyph may carry a distinct semantic/structural move, but that move must stay inside the shared wordmark grammar and cannot introduce a second visual style.

correctness_guard.rule: Key Chinese recognition skeletons, radicals and signature strokes must remain unambiguous. Correctness is a hard constraint, not an aesthetic variable.
correctness_guard.technical_retry_policy: A wrong/unreadable character is technical invalid. Taste weakness is not technical invalid.

hard_avoids: designing each character independently and combining them afterward
one glyph organic and the paired glyph industrial unless a shared stroke genome visibly unifies them
stretching as the primary design move
decorative beams or blocks that do not belong to the character system
surface distress used to disguise weak structure
copying exact Shanyeji contours, missing-stroke locations or brand assets

test_surface.baseline: Reuse the already-frozen strong Candidate 1 baseline for each title; do not regenerate or weaken it.
test_surface.new_candidate: Create one new V2 wordmark-first Candidate 2 per title.

bounded_budget.technical_retries: Only for objective wrong/unreadable glyphs; must not be used to hide taste failure.

questions: Can the title be read immediately and unambiguously?
Do both characters visibly belong to one wordmark system rather than two styles assembled together?
Is the new Candidate 2 materially more designed than the frozen strong Candidate 1 baseline?
Does the authored quality move meaningfully toward the approved Shanyeji mother-reference level, even without copying its exact forms?
human_gate.pass: Both 豆坊 and 茶作 must pass correctness and wordmark coherence, and both must be human-preferred to the frozen strong baseline for authored design quality.
human_gate.fail: If the wordmark-first candidate still lacks coherence or remains only marginally more designed than the baseline after the bounded correction, stop V2 and do not enter T2.
